import cv2
import numpy as np
from triangulate import get_bearing, intersect_rays
from check_ground_contact_close import ground_point

# Plant 2 in obs_0016:
# In obs_0016 (pose: x=-0.683, y=2.183, h=300):
# Plant 2 is on the left edge: u ~ 18.1
# In obs_0006 (pose: x=0, y=0, h=300): u ~ 292.1
print("Plant 2 (6 & 16):", intersect_rays(*get_bearing(6, 292.1), *get_bearing(16, 18.1)))

# In obs_0039: (pose: x=0.920, y=3.970, h=240)
# Looking along heading 240 deg (towards negative x, negative y)
# There are TWO plants in obs_0039!
# Left plant in obs_0039: u ~ 238, v bottom ~ 345
# Right plant in obs_0039: u ~ 394.6, v bottom ~ 392
# Wait! In heading 240 from (0.92, 3.97):
# Bearing of u=238 is: 240 + atan2(238-255.5, 256) = 240 - 3.9 = 236.1 deg.
# Bearing of u=395 is: 240 + atan2(395-255.5, 256) = 240 + 28.6 = 268.6 deg.
# The right plant is towards negative x, same y (270 deg is due west / -x)!
# That's at y ~ 3.9, x < 0. That's Plant 1 at (-2.68, 3.83)!
# The LEFT plant in 39 is towards 236 deg (south-west), which is Plant 2!
print("Plant 1 pos from 39 ground contact:", ground_point(39, 394.6, 392))
# Let's check the LEFT plant in 39:
img39 = cv2.imread('/work/observations/obs_0039.png')
pot_mask39_p2 = (img39[:, :, 2] > 140) & (img39[:, :, 0] < 80) & (img39[:, :, 1] < 120)
pot_mask39_p2[:, 300:] = 0
ys, xs = np.where(pot_mask39_p2)
print(f"Plant 2 in 39: bottom v={ys.max()}, center u={np.mean(xs):.1f}")
print("Plant 2 pos from 39 left plant:", ground_point(39, np.mean(xs), ys.max()))
